snacks.tip: Potassium against cramps. Bring single sachets.

snacks.tip: In a lidded box. Crunchy, hydrating and mess-free.

snacks.name: Apple

snacks.name: Boiled eggs
snacks.tip: Boil 6 on Sunday. Cheap, practical protein.

snacks.name: Homemade oat bar

snacks.name: Cheese cubes + wholegrain toast

nutri.iaTitle: Tell me where you are or what you have
nutri.placeholder: e.g. I'm at a highway gas station…

posto.title: At the gas station
items: Small cheese bread + unsweetened coffee
Coconut water or mineral water (skip soda)
Banana or apple from the shelf
If there's a buffet: rice, beans, grilled protein and salad
posto.hydration: Buy 1.5L of water now. Goal: one sip at every traffic light.

padaria.title: At the bakery
items: Wholegrain bread with scrambled eggs
Plain yogurt with granola
Fresh juice with no sugar
Skip fried pastries — they weigh you down while driving
padaria.hydration: Ask for a glass of water with your coffee. Coffee doesn't count as hydration.

lanchonete.title: At the fast food place
items: Grilled chicken sandwich, no mayo
Swap fries for salad or corn
Water or fresh juice instead of soda
Eat slowly: 15 min parked beats eating while driving
lanchonete.hydration: Soda dehydrates. Ask for water with lemon.

maos.title: With what you have
items: Build a plate: {{input}} + a fiber source (salad or fruit)
Protein first, carbs later: less post-lunch sleepiness
Carb portion the size of your closed fist
Save half if you're too full — it's your 4pm snack
maos.hydration: Drink a glass of water before eating. It helps with fullness.

default.title: Smart choice for right now
items: Prioritize: lean protein + veggies + whole carbs
Avoid fried food and sugar before long drives
If there's only a corner store: yogurt, fruit, nuts and water
Eat every 3–4h to stay alert at the wheel
default.hydration: Daily goal: 2 to 3 liters. Keep a bottle visible on the dashboard.

lift.title: How to Lift Heavy Boxes
lift.subtitle: 16 essential ergonomic techniques
tabsLong: Set the load down and prevent injuries

tips.d: Gently push the box with your foot or hand to test the weight before pulling.
Feet shoulder-width apart with one foot slightly forward for balance.
Bend your knees and hips. Never round your lower back.
Hold the package against your belly/chest; holding it away multiplies the force on your spine.
Fit your palms on the lower diagonal corners of the box (not just fingertips).
Lift by pushing the floor with your thighs and glutes, breathing out as you rise.
Never twist your spine while holding weight; turn your body by moving your feet.
Keep chin and chest up while walking with the load.
Always climb using 3 points of contact; never jump with boxes in your arms.
For deep compartments, rest the box edge on the sill/shelf and slide it in.
Keep heavy items stored between thigh and chest height in the van.
When taking boxes from above shoulder height, get close and never arch your back.
Reverse the movement to set the load down: bend your legs and lower with a straight torso.
Use the box corners as leverage and bend your knees wider.
Be careful not to drop heavy boxes on your toes or trip on loose cables.
If the weight makes you compensate with your neck or spine, stop, use a trolley or ask for help.

post.name: Lower Back Release
post.d: Kneel on a mat, sit back on your heels and reach your arms forward, forehead down. Breathe slowly.

post.name: Leg Relief
post.d: Lie with your hips near a wall and stretch your legs up. Helps circulation and reduces swelling.

post.name: Trapezius & Neck
post.d: Tilt your head to the side and let your hand's weight gently pull. 30s each side.

post.name: Glutes & Sciatic
post.d: Seated or lying, cross your ankle over the opposite knee and bring the leg toward your chest.
